title: Identifiability of Parent Registration Data
description: Registration data (email, name, govt ID) collected from parent user can be used to identify the individual. This PII collection creates inherent identifiability risk.
assumptions: Data is stored and processed in a manner that preserves identifying information

title: Disclosure of Sensitive Registration Data
description: Sensitive data including password, government ID, and personal information could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during transmission or storage.
assumptions: Authentication service may not have adequate security controls for data protection

title: Linkability of Registration Data to Other Data Sources
description: Email, name, and government ID can be linked to other data sources (e.g., other services, public records) creating comprehensive user profiles.
assumptions: Data may be shared or accessible across multiple systems

title: Usurpation via Registration Data
description: Collected registration data (especially government ID and email) could be misused for identity theft or impersonation of the parent user.
assumptions: Data could be intercepted or accessed by malicious actors

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Parent Account Data
description: MongoDB users collection may be accessed by unauthorized parties, leading to disclosure of parent account information. This violates the minimality principle and creates privacy risks for stored personal data.

title: Unauthorized Modification of Parent Account Data
description: Stored parent account data in MongoDB could be modified without authorization, compromising data integrity and potentially leading to identity fraud or account takeover.

title: Direct Identification via Parent Account Information
description: Parent account data inherently contains personally identifiable information that can directly identify individuals, creating identification privacy risks.

title: Linkability Across Systems via Parent Account Data
description: Parent account information stored by the authentication service could be linked to other user activities or external systems, enabling cross-system tracking and profiling.

title: Authentication Service Compromise Leading to Identity Usurpation
description: If the authentication service is compromised, attackers could potentially impersonate users or gain unauthorized access to parent account data, enabling identity usurpation.

title: Linkability of JWT tokens across systems
description: JWT tokens transmitted from Authentication Service to Parent User may be linked to other data flows or systems, enabling correlation of user activities across different contexts.
assumptions: JWT tokens contain identifiable user information that can be correlated with other data sources

title: Identifiability of user data in transmission

title: Child login linked to parent identity via parent email
